messages:
sophia (Intern): Hey team — quick Q about PTO for interns: I started mid-June, how is accrual prorated? Also wondering if interns can carry over unused days to fall?

maria (People Ops): Welcome on the team, Sophia! For summer interns we prorate PTO based on full months worked. Policy: 1 day accrues per full month worked (so if you started 6/15 that's not a full month). No automatic carryover for interns — balances expire at the end of the internship contract unless an extension is approved.

sophia (Intern): Ah got it — so starting 6/15 means 0 days for June and 1 day for July, etc?

maria (People Ops): Correct. We count the first full calendar month after your start date. If your internship extends past the originally scheduled end date, managers can request an exception to convert unused days to paid time for the extended period, but it needs People Ops sign-off.

kevin (Eng Manager): For planning — if we want to give interns a bridge day during the company summer shutdown week, is that something managers can mandate, or do we need to treat it as paid time off from their prorated balance?

maria (People Ops): Good question. Two options: 1) If the intern's contract includes the company shutdown week, treat it like a company-paid holiday (no PTO cost) — People Ops & legal need to confirm in the offer. 2) If not included, the day comes out of prorated PTO. Managers should check the intern's offer letters and ping People Ops before marking comp time.

kevin (Eng Manager): Sounds reasonable. For interns that join on short notice, is there any ability to front-load a small PTO allotment so they don't feel stuck?

amaria (People Ops): We try to avoid front-loading for short internships because accrual/repayment logistics get messy. Exception can be made in exceptional circumstances — require manager + People Ops approval and note in the HR record.

alex (People Ops): To add — if a manager requests an exception we need: intern name, start/end dates, requested PTO front-load amount, reason, and manager approval email. Send to people-ops@redwood.com and we'll review.

hr-bot: Reminder: please submit any PTO exceptions at least 7 business days before the requested time off so payroll and scheduling can be coordinated. :bell:

_tim (Payroll): FYI on the payroll side — when an exception is approved we code the payout/adjustment to the contractor/intern ledger under "Intern PTO Adjustments". We need the approval email to attach to the payroll ticket. If an intern leaves before accruing the days, we prorate final payment per the exception approval.

sophia (Intern): Thanks everyone — super helpful. I'll check my offer and ping Maria if needed. :thumbsup:

maria (People Ops): Anytime! Link to intern PTO docs: https://intranet.redwood.com/hr/intern-pto (please read before asking managers to approve anything).
